headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API document ingestion can feed Pathway pipelines, creating default-path prompt-injection and data-handling exposure, but no direct shared-write or action-taking channel is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP Server plus API surfaces, so its outputs can carry attacker-controlled document text. Pathway is a data-pipeline framework with no documented verification layer here, so if it consumes MinerU output as input, prompt-like content can propagate. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests MinerU-extracted text without sanitization or provenance tags
IF MinerU processes untrusted documents containing instruction-like content
mitigations: Add a provenance field to MinerU outputs before passing them onward
Filter or strip instruction-like strings from extracted text
Require Pathway to treat MinerU output as data, not instructions
Run a one-document test with a malicious prompt embedded in a PDF
requires-engineering: add schema validation between MinerU and Pathway

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, so sensitive document content can enter its processing flow. Pathway’s profile shows no file surfaces or egress, but its pipeline role means it may receive that content downstream. Because the shared-workspace or upload path is undocumented, leakage is plausible but not proven, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents and forwards extracted text to Pathway
IF Pathway is deployed with any downstream sink that persists or republishes MinerU output
mitigations: Classify inputs before sending them to MinerU
Redact secrets from extracted text before handoff
Keep MinerU and Pathway on separate workspaces
Verify whether Pathway persists intermediate records
requires-engineering: enforce field-level access controls on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU has no filesystem write, shell, subprocess, or git modification capability, and Pathway likewise shows no write, shell, or git capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource access documented, there is no plausible write-write conflict pathway in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF either profile later gains write access to the same directory or git repo
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Separate any writable staging areas
Avoid mounting a shared mutable repository
requires-engineering: add locking if write access is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted document text and structured fields, while Pathway is a pipeline framework that may consume and transform those outputs. If Pathway treats MinerU output as authoritative without validation, extraction errors can cascade into downstream analytics or actions. No explicit verification or human review is documented, so the interaction is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF Pathway uses MinerU output as a source of truth without validation
IF downstream jobs act on extracted fields for reporting or routing
mitigations: Add a validation step after MinerU extraction
Sample-check a few outputs against source documents
Mark extracted fields as untrusted until verified
Log extraction confidence or provenance
requires-engineering: build a reconciliation workflow for disputed fields

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source document-processing tools with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. MinerU touches many document classes, but Pathway’s profile does not show regulated-data handling or a conflicting compliance posture. With no concrete mismatch evidence, the compliance risk is low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through MinerU and then stored by Pathway under different retention rules
mitigations: Document the data classes sent to each agent
Align retention settings before deployment
Avoid sending regulated documents through the pair
Review vendor compliance claims separately
requires-engineering: add a retention policy gate
